title: Geometric dictionary for stalk and infinitesimal quotient cohomology
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $\mathcal F$ coherent [pqf-def-coherent], $y\in Y$ and $p\ge0$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$, $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ the canonical map [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], $X'=\operatorname{Spec}A\times_YX$ with projections $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, $g':X'\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X'}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] and let $C$ be $H^p(X',-)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] regarded as an $A$-module by $A\to\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$. Put $M=(R^pf_*\mathcal F)_y$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $Q_n=C(\mathcal F'/J^{n+1}\mathcal F')$ with its quotient transitions [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], and $B_n=H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ with the canonical transitions and scalar actions [def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology]. Then $\mathcal F'$ is coherent, and there exist an $A$-linear equivalence $a:M\to C(\mathcal F')$, an isomorphism of inverse systems $b:Q\to B$ after restricting scalars from $\widehat A$ to $A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $A$-linear maps $\kappa_n:M\to B_n$ satisfying IsFormalFunctionsTheta [def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology], such that $\kappa_n(z)=b_n(C(q_n)(a(z)))$ for every $n\ge0$ and $z\in M$, where $q_n:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'/J^{n+1}\mathcal F'$ is the quotient projection. This assertion concerns uncompleted cohomology and finite-level quotient systems; it asserts no isomorphism involving a completed cohomology module or a limit.

source.place: Tag 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk), proof before the final application of Theorem 02OC, coherent.tex lines 5759-5798; Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), Tag 01E4 and Tag 089W. The omitted identifications and transition compatibilities are expanded in steps 1-7 of lem-weil-pbc-formal-functions-stalk.

proof.text: (The local ring and the canonical morphism.) Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$. As $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $y$ lies in an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian, and $A\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; so $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $c:Y'\to Y$ be the canonical morphism and $y'$ the closed point of $Y'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]: $c$ is flat, $c(y')=y$, $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$ for every open $V\ni y$, the stalk map $\mathcal G_y\to(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is an isomorphism for every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$, and $c_n=c\circ c'_n$ with $c'_n:\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)\to Y'$ the closed immersion given by the quotient map (part (5) with $J=\mathfrak m^n$). This is 'c is a flat morphism as it identifies local rings' and the hint 'the morphisms $c_n$ factor through $c$' of the source. In Lean the Noetherian stalk ring is provided by the Mathlib instance for a locally Noetherian scheme.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (The base change.) Let $X'=Y'\times_YX$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $f'$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), hence of finite type, so $X'$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] (Step 1). $\mathcal F$ is coherent on the locally Noetherian $X$ ([pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] for $f$), hence quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; so $\mathcal F'$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (3), hence coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Also $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (finite type and separated, [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Since $c(Y')\subseteq V$ for every open $V\ni y$ (Step 1), $g'(X')\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and $f'^{-1}(c^{-1}V)=X'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (The stalk is $H^p(X',\mathcal F')$.) Define $\varphi:M\to H:=H^p(X',\mathcal F')$ by $\varphi([\xi]_V)=(g'_V)^*\xi$ for $\xi\in H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$, where $g'_V:X'\to f^{-1}(V)$ is $g'$ (Step 2) and $(g'_V)^*$ the pullback [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) (with $(g'_V)^*(\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}V})=\mathcal F'$); it is well defined because pullback commutes with restriction to smaller $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2),(3), and $A$-linear, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ acting on $H$ through $A=\Gamma(Y',\mathcal O_{Y'})\to\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ (linearity in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], $c^\sharp$ inducing the identity of $A$ on stalks, Step 1). $\varphi$ is bijective: let $G=R^pf_*\mathcal F$ and $G'=R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$. By flat base change [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] ($c$ flat, $f$ qcqs, $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent) the base change map $\beta:c^*G\to G'$ is an isomorphism ($g'$ is flat as a base change of $c$, so the base change map of Stacks 02N7 is defined). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-map-sections] its adjoint $\beta^\flat=c_*(\beta)\circ\eta_G:G\to c_*G'$ sends $[\xi]_V$ to the class of $(g'_V)^*\xi$ in $G'(c^{-1}V)=G'(Y')$. Take stalks: the composite $G_y\to(c^*G)_{y'}\xrightarrow{\beta_{y'}}G'_{y'}$, whose first arrow is the isomorphism of Step 1 (germ of the unit $\eta_G$), sends $[\xi]_V$ to the germ at $y'$ of the class of $(g'_V)^*\xi$, so it is an isomorphism. Finally $G_y=M$ and $G'_{y'}=\varinjlim_{W\ni y'}H^p(f'^{-1}W,\mathcal F')=H^p(X',\mathcal F')$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf], [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], since $Y'$ is the only open of $Y'$ containing the closed point $y'$ of the local scheme (an open containing $\mathfrak m$ contains every prime of $A$, all being generalizations of $\mathfrak m$). Under these identifications the composite is $\varphi$; hence $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules (Stacks: $c^*R^pf_*\mathcal F=R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$ by 02KH, and $(R^pf'_*\mathcal F')_{y'}=\Gamma(Y',R^pf'_*\mathcal F')=H^p(X',\mathcal F')$; the stalk route used here avoids the affine-base lemma 01XK). (Linearity and the degree-0 description of these maps: [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties].)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800); Lemma 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology) and Cohomology Lemma 02N7 (base change map)

proof.text: (The infinitesimal neighbourhoods are identified.) Let $p_n:X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)$ be the second projection. Since $f\circ i_n=c_n\circ p_n=c\circ c'_n\circ p_n$ (Step 1), the universal property of $X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a unique $i'_n:X_n\to X'$ with $g'\circ i'_n=i_n$ and $f'\circ i'_n=c'_n\circ p_n$, and $(X_n,i'_n,p_n)$ is a fibre product $X'\times_{Y'}\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)$ (pasting of the two cartesian squares, by the universal properties). Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (1),(2) for $f'$ and $K=\mathfrak m^n$, $i'_n$ is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathfrak m^n\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I^n$, $\mathcal I=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X'}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $i'_n$ is affine (preimages of affine opens are affine) [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; by its part (3) the transition closed immersion $j_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ satisfies $i'_{n+1}\circ j_n=i'_n$ (uniqueness in the universal property of $X'$, as $g'i'_{n+1}j_n=i_{n+1}j_n=i_n$). Moreover $\mathcal F_n=i_n^*\mathcal F=(g'\circ i'_n)^*\mathcal F\cong i'^*_n\mathcal F'$ canonically [def-pc-module-pullback], and $\mathcal F_n$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. ('The infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the fibre $X_y$ and $X'_y$ are identified (verification omitted)' in the source.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (The maps $\theta_n$ factor through $\varphi$.) Let $u_n:\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ be the $i'_n$-map adjoint to the isomorphism $i'^*_n\mathcal F'\cong\mathcal F_n$ (the unit $\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}i'^*_n\mathcal F'$ followed by it), and $\theta'_n=u_n^*:H\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$, i.e. the pullback along $i'_n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. By definition $\theta_n([\xi]_V)$ is the pullback of $\xi$ along $i_n:X_n\to f^{-1}(V)$, which is $i_n=g'_V\circ i'_n$; by [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2) (and the compatibility of the canonical isomorphisms $(g'i'_n)^*\cong i'^*_ng'^*$ with the units [def-pc-module-pullback]) $\theta_n=\theta'_n\circ\varphi$. Likewise $i'_n=i'_{n+1}\circ j_n$ gives $\tau_n\circ\theta'_{n+1}=\theta'_n$ for the transition maps $\tau_n:H^p(X_{n+1},\mathcal F_{n+1})\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ of the statement, so the $\theta_n$ are compatible with the transition maps. All these maps are $A$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], and $A$ acts on $H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ through $A\to\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, which factors through $A/\mathfrak m^n$ ($f'\circ i'_n=c'_n\circ p_n$); hence $\theta_n$ vanishes on $\mathfrak m^nM$ and $\theta'_n$ on $\mathfrak m^nH$. (Linearity and the degree-0 description of these maps: [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties].)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (Cohomology of $X_n$ as cohomology on $X'$.) Let $q_n:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'$ be the quotient map (notation of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0)). Since $i'_n$ is a closed immersion with ideal $\mathcal I^n$ (Step 4), the unit $\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}i'^*_n\mathcal F'$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient]; composing with $i'_{n*}$ of $i'^*_n\mathcal F'\cong\mathcal F_n$ gives an isomorphism $\rho_n:\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ with $\rho_n\circ q_n=u_n$ ('$i_{n,*}\mathcal F_n=i_{n,*}i_n^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F/\mathfrak m^n\mathcal F$' in the source). As $i'_n$ is affine and $\mathcal F_n$ quasi-coherent (Step 4), the edge map $e_n:H^p(X',i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n)\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] ('by the Leray spectral sequence for $i_n$' in the source). Put $\psi_n=e_n\circ H^p(\rho_n):H^p(X',\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2), $\psi_n=\rho_n^*$ is the map of the $i'_n$-map $\rho_n$ and $\psi_n\circ H^p(q_n)=(\rho_n\circ q_n)^*=u_n^*=\theta'_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800); Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology) for the Leray step

proof.text: (The $\psi_n$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems.) Let $\pi_n:\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'$ be the transition map ($\pi_n\circ q_{n+1}=q_n$) and $t_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to j_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ the $j_n$-map defining $\tau_n=t_n^*$ (Step 5). By [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2), $\tau_n\circ\psi_{n+1}$ is the map of the $i'_n$-map $a=i'_{n+1,*}(t_n)\circ\rho_{n+1}$ and $\psi_n\circ H^p(\pi_n)$ that of $b=\rho_n\circ\pi_n$, both morphisms $\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n$. Now $b\circ q_{n+1}=\rho_n\circ q_n=u_n$, and $a\circ q_{n+1}=i'_{n+1,*}(t_n)\circ u_{n+1}$, which is the $i'_n$-map adjoint to the composite of the canonical isomorphisms $i'^*_n\mathcal F'\cong j_n^*i'^*_{n+1}\mathcal F'\cong j_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$, i.e. again $u_n$ (the canonical isomorphisms of iterated pullbacks are compatible [def-pc-module-pullback]). Since $q_{n+1}$ is an epimorphism, $a=b$, so $\tau_n\circ\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ H^p(\pi_n)$: $(\psi_n)_n$ is an isomorphism of inverse systems from $(H^p(X',\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'))_n$ to $(H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n))_n$, and $\varprojlim\psi_n$ is an isomorphism. (This is the compatibility the source leaves implicit in 'hence we may indeed apply the theorem on formal functions to compute the limit'.) Restrict the completed scalar action to A; its evaluation on algebraMap(A, A-completion) is the canonical quotient map. Thus these identifications form the A-linear natural isomorphism b in the statement. The maps kappa_n are the original canonical stalk pullbacks, and steps 3, 5 and 6 give kappa_n(z) = b_n(H^p(q_n)(a(z))). No completion comparison is used.

lean.statement: theorem formalFunctions_local_dictionary {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (F : X.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F) (y : Y) (p : ℕ) : let X' := pullback (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f let f' := pullback.fst (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f let F' := (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd (Y.fromSpecStalk y) f)).obj F let J := (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop ((maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y)).map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of (Y.presheaf.stalk y))).inv.hom)).comap f' let C := RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X'.toRingedSpace p ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of (Y.presheaf.stalk y))).inv ≫ f'.appTop).hom RingedSpace.IsCoherent X'.toRingedSpace F' ∧ ∃ a : formalFunctionsStalk f y F p ≃ₗ[Y.presheaf.stalk y] C.obj F', ∃ b : formalCompletionSystem J F' ⋙ C ≅ formalFibreCohomologySystem f y F p ⋙ ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap (Y.presheaf.stalk y) (AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y))), ∃ κ : ∀ n : ℕ, formalFunctionsStalk f y F p →ₗ[Y.presheaf.stalk y] formalFibreCohomologyLocal f y F p n, (∀ n : ℕ, IsFormalFunctionsTheta f y F p n (κ n)) ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : formalFunctionsStalk f y F p), κ n z = (b.hom.app (op n)) ((C.map (formalModuleQuotientπ J (n + 1) F')) (a z))
